summary: The candidate spent the full ten minutes reading files and narrating fragments of code-tracing (stockLedger, expiryIndex, reservationService, holdStore) without ever forming a concrete hypothesis about the defect mechanism, and asked the interviewer for hints twice rather than resolving the ambiguity themselves. No code was edited and no fix was attempted; the session ended with the candidate explicitly giving up.

dimensions.analysis: The candidate described the failing assertion as expecting 10 but receiving 6, which does not match the actual defect (a held-units-not-released-at-exact-expiry issue), suggesting they never carefully pinned down what the test was actually asserting. Rather than resolving this by re-reading the test or spec, they twice asked the interviewer directly for a hint on where the bug lived instead of narrowing the ambiguity themselves.

The stated intentions never rose above vague location-hunting — wanting to find 'the entry point' or figure out 'where we're setting available units' — with no articulation of a mechanism such as a boundary condition in the expiry sweep or index. Even after opening expiryIndex.ts multiple times, no hypothesis about binary-search boundaries or tie-handling was ever voiced.

Long stretches of file-opening produced little accompanying narration, and much of the audible speech was filler, laughter, or off-topic asides rather than reasoning about the code, making the transcript alone insufficient to reconstruct their thinking. Even where narration existed (e.g. tracing available units through the ledger), it stayed descriptive rather than diagnostic, and never connected observations into a working theory.
No code edits were made at any point in the session — only file reads are recorded — so there is nothing to assess against a stated plan.
Since no fix was ever attempted, there was no artifact to verify; the only test run was the initial failing run at the start of the session.

When directly asked for a final fix and rationale, the candidate explicitly gave up rather than offering any explanation of the failure mechanism or even a partial theory, despite having had the opportunity across multiple nudges to synthesize one.
